theorem_title: The query word bound fits its uniform envelope
theorem_formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.SharedReportingBankResourceBounds.query_word_le (n : ℕ) :
    _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.SharedReportingBankResourceBounds.queryWord (_root_.ThreeSum.SharedReportingBankResourceBounds.half n) (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.SharedReportingBankResourceBounds.blocks n) (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BandScales.bandSize n) ≤ _root_.ThreeSum.SharedReportingBankResourceBounds.queryEnvelope n := by sorry
theorem_natural_language_statement:
For every natural input size $n$, evaluate the local half-size $h(n)$, block count $J(n)$, and band width $g(n)$ at their executable values. Then $$\operatorname{queryWord}(h(n),J(n),g(n))\le\operatorname{queryEnvelope}(n).$$

Bounds the actual query arithmetic independently of stored absolute pointers. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
